meanings: The Legends of Rivenkeep: the Book's title page ('the tales of the holding-place of the cleft')

derivation: a phrase: sull 'three' + tolm 'a stone' (canon; a numeral before a singular noun, orrowen_v2 §3.1) + ul susk 'above, over' (O2638) + et odh 'the hearth' (canon) [wf12 unit S11]

meanings: on both sides, from either side ('shoulder and shoulder'): hy sest eth sest et myst, from both sides of the grey (Book Four's Argument)
derivation: a phrase: sest 'the shoulder; a side' (reserve, O2284) + eth 'and' + sest, the distributive X eth X (O2862 hos eth hos, O2926 trenn eth trenn); hy pa sest would soften pa to va and be heard 'from your side' [wf12 unit S11]

meanings: Hold the stone, Seren: Seren's opening of a telling of her own (v3: I.4, II.1, IV.1, V.1, V.2, V.7, VI.3, the Epilogue, the Last Note)
derivation: a phrase: canon Keth et tolm 'Hold the stone' (Halyna to the child Seren, orrowen_v2 §11.11; the Invocation's close, §11.10) + Seren, called by name (the vocative softens; s is unchanged) [wf12 unit S11]

meanings: a flat grey stone; et sull tolm ryss myst, the three grey stones of the Mystaeri over Elspet's fire and, after the homecomings, over the Long Hearth (IV.5, VI.1, the Last Note); never tolm myst side by side, which is Myststone
derivation: a phrase: canon tolm 'a stone' + ryss 'wide; flat' (reserve) + myst '(adj.) grey' (canon), the adjectives after the noun; ryss keeps tolm and myst apart (the v1.3 unit S06's phrase, orrowen_v2 §4.7) [wf12 unit S11]

meanings: the haft of a mallet ('the staff of a mallet'): hosen hulter runn hemm, 'like the haft of an old mallet' (the Book of Knowings)

meanings: last night ('yesterday, at night')

meanings: curling signs, curling letters ('signs curled'): the Mystaeri letters as the Shore sees them and cannot read them: IV.1's stones cut ul rellorath kylet, 'with curling letters', and the Last Note's rellorath kylet lo dhrenn et cless, 'the curling letters along its edge'
